newsitem.title: FRANCE: Moulinex narrows H1 loss, unclear on future.
newsitem.headline: Moulinex narrows H1 loss, unclear on future.

text.p: French appliance maker Moulinex reduced losses in the first half of its 1996/97 year by 38 percent but said on Friday that the benefits of a restructuring programme would not come through until 1997/98.
It said its net attributable loss narrowed to 74 million french francs ($14 million) in the six months to September 30 from 121 million.

Operating loss decreased to nine million francs from a loss of 99 million, reflecting a drop in raw materials costs and favourable currency trends. Its financial costs dropped 40 percent to 41 million francs due to lower French interest rates.
In the 1995/96 year to March 31, Moulinex reported a loss of 702 million francs, its fourth consecutive annual loss, after taking a 600 million franc charge for the restructuring plan.
Chairman Pierre Blayau told an analysts' meeting that as the first-half improvement was due mainly to external factors, he was reluctant to predict a trend for the second half.
"We're cautious in our outlook for the year," he said.
He said he did not expect to see before 1997/98 tangible results of a restructuring plan unveiled in June.

The company cautioned that business in October and November was hurt by a truckers' strike in France that disrupted deliveries, and weak consumer spending in Europe. "The market looks much worse in the second half than in the first," he said.
Moulinex said the difficult climate required the introduction of short-time working at some plants and make it imperative to go ahead with the restructuring plan.
The company is concluding a six-month consultations with employees who oppose measures to cut 2,600 jobs, or more than 20 percent of the staff, and close two plants.
About 2,100 jobs will be cut in France and the rest in Germany, where layoffs have begun.

The company plans to push ahead with the restructuring, but Blayau said management would begin negotiations on January 8 to save up to 750 jobs by reducing work hours. He said he hoped for a job-saving agreement by January 20.
He said the company planned a 500 million franc capital increase in the first quarter of 1997 to strengthen its balance sheet. The terms will be announced in early 1997.
Moulinex's debt stands at 1.76 billion francs, down from 1.92 billion a year ago, but its equity has shrunk to 697 million francs from 1.28 billion.

The company aims to reduce stocks, which it considers too high at 1.89 billion francs, increase its presence outside Europe while maintaining its market share in its regional market and launch new appliances next year to freshen its product line. ($1=5.260 French Franc)
